docsHtml:
HiGHS Web Modeler: Getting Started & Python Migration Guide

HiGHS Web Modeler is a modern modeling library powered by the world-class mathematical optimization solver HiGHS (WebAssembly) from the University of Edinburgh. It brings the intuitive, elegant modeling experience familiar from Python's PuLP and python-mip directly to browser and Node.js environments.

Package Installation & Runtime Environments

npm / pnpm / bun (Package Installation Example)
npm install @ohtaman/washi
Standard Browser ESM (Pre-built Distribution)
<script type="module">
  // Host and serve dist/browser bundle from your web server
  import { Model, expr, maximize } from "./dist/browser/washi.js";

  const m = new Model("Production");
  const x = m.integer("x", { lb: 0 });
  const y = m.integer("y", { lb: 0 });

  m.objective(maximize(expr\`30 * \${x} + 50 * \${y}\`));
  m.constraint(expr\`\${x} + 2 * \${y} <= 40\`, "c1");
  m.constraint(expr\`2 * \${x} + \${y} <= 50\`, "c2");

  const status = await m.solve({ useWorker: false });
  console.log("Optimal objective value:", m.objectiveValue); // 1100
  console.log("x:", x.value, "y:", y.value);     // 20, 10
</script>

Distribution & Offline Usage

When integrated via Vite or webpack from npm, bundled WASM and Worker files are emitted directly as build assets without external CDN dependencies. For direct browser usage, host and serve the dist/browser bundle via HTTP. Once assets are loaded locally, optimization runs completely offline.

In CodePen, add the hosted dist/browser/washi.min.js URL under External Scripts and instantiate via Washi.Model. Basic models run synchronously with solve({ useWorker: false }). Worker threads require proper CORS and CSP setup.

Z3 Solver & Browser Security Requirements (Cross-Origin Isolation)

The Z3 SMT / MIP solver operates on multi-threaded WebAssembly (SharedArrayBuffer). Under browser security specifications, the following document response headers are mandatory:

Required HTTP Response Headers
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp

On static hosting where custom response headers cannot be configured (e.g. GitHub Pages) or CodePen previews, Z3 cannot run without an isolation polyfill. In this official Web showcase (hosted on GitHub Pages), an isolated coi-serviceworker.js scoped to /washi/ is registered on same-origin to provide a seamless crossOriginIsolated runtime via a single controlled reload. (*Importing the core library @ohtaman/washi never automatically registers a Service Worker on host applications.)

WaSHI Modern Algebraic Modeling API Quick Reference

Modeling Construct WaSHI API (TypeScript / JS) 説明
Model Initialization const m = new Model("Name"); Create optimization model. Defaults to HiGHS (WASM) solver.
Binary Variables m.binary("x") / m.binary(items) 0-1 decision variables. Multidimensional naming and array tensors supported.
Integer Variables m.integer("x", { lb: 0, ub: 10 }) Integer decision variables with configurable lower and upper bounds.
Continuous Variables m.continuous("x", { lb: 0 }) Continuous decision variables for linear and quadratic programming.
Expressions & Constraints expr\`30 * \${x} + 50 * \${y}\` / expr\`\${x} + 2 * \${y} <= 40\` Arithmetic expressions and relational constraints via tagged template DSL (expr).
Constraint Addition m.constraint(expr\`...\`, "name") Declarative constraint registration; accepts single constraints or collections.
Objective Function m.objective(maximize(...)) / m.objective(minimize(...)) Set objective function and sense via explicit combinators (maximize / minimize).
Summation & Inner Products sum(items, i => x[i]) / dot(costs, x) Functional summation and linear algebra dot-product aggregations.
Solve & Optimization await m.solve() Execute optimization solve routine via WebAssembly solver backend.
Conflict Diagnosis (Unsat Core) m.conflicts / res.conflicts Extract minimal unsatisfiable constraint subset when model is infeasible.
Solution Extraction x.value / m.getValues([x, y]) Retrieve optimal variable values or bulk dictionaries and matrices.

Key Architectural Capabilities

  • Asynchronous Web Worker Execution: Even large-scale mixed-integer programs (MIP) execute on dedicated worker threads, preventing UI lockups.
  • Tagged Template DSL: Construct ASTs directly from mathematical strings like expr\`\${x} + 2 * \${y} <= 40\` with type-safe binding.
  • CPLEX LP Standard Compliance: Export full LP model text via m.toLpString() for seamless interoperability with HiGHS, Gurobi, CPLEX, SCIP, and GLPK.
  • Dual Variables & Reduced Costs: Built-in sensitivity analysis via constraint.dual (shadow prices) and var.reducedCost.
  • Multidimensional Variable Matrices: Define multidimensional decision tensors via m.binary(rows, cols) for transportation and assignment problems.
  • Pluggable Solver Independence: Seamlessly switch solvers via m.solve(new HiGHS()), MockSolver, or custom optimization backends.

Solver Independence & Injection

Model formulation and solver engine execution are completely decoupled.

Solver Switching Example
import { Model, HiGHS, MockSolver, generateLpString } from "@ohtaman/washi";

// 1. Solve with default HiGHS WebAssembly solver
await m.solve();

// 2. Solve with configured HiGHS instance
await m.solve(new HiGHS({ timeLimit: 30, mipGap: 0.01 }));

// 3. Mock solver for unit tests / CI without WASM overhead
await m.solve(new MockSolver({
  status: "Optimal",
  values: { x: 10, y: 20 },
  objectiveValue: 100
}));

// 4. Custom backend server injection via Solver interface
const myBackendSolver = {
  name: "CompanyOptAPI",
  async solve(modelData) {
    // Generate LP string and POST to optimization microservice
    const { lpString } = generateLpString(modelData);
    const res = await fetch("/api/v1/solve", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ lp: lpString }),
    });
    const data = await res.json();
    return { status: data.status, objectiveValue: data.obj, values: data.solution };
  }
};
await m.solve(myBackendSolver);
